🚨 JUST IN: The first Tesla Semi has rolled off the new high-volume production line at the dedicated factory in Nevada! 🎉
Huge milestone for electric trucking. Tesla is ramping toward volume production in 2026, with a target capacity of up to 50,000 units per year at the Giga Semi facility next to Giga Nevada.
Key Facts about the Tesla Semi:
•  Two variants:
•  Standard Range: ~325 miles range at full 82,000 lb GCW.
•  Long Range: ~500 miles range (at 82k lb GCW).
•  Powertrain: 3 independent electric motors on rear axles, up to 800 kW drive power.
•  Efficiency: ~1.7 kWh per mile — dramatically lower operating costs vs. diesel (often 60-70% savings).
•  Charging: Megawatt Charging System (MCS), up to 1.2 MW, ~60% range in 30 minutes.
•  Other highlights: Autonomy-ready, ePTO, strong acceleration/safety (regenerative braking), and designed for million-mile durability.
This is a game-changer for Class 8 trucking: zero emissions, lower TCO, and massive scalability. Congrats to the Tesla Semi team! ⚡🚛

Day 3 of the Musk vs. OpenAI trial just got spicy. 🔥

OpenAI’s lawyer William Savitt tried to paint Elon as some kind of small-time donor who didn’t deliver on his big promises hammering him on the $38 million actually given versus the “up to $1 billion” he once floated.

Elon wasn’t having it.

“Without me, OpenAI wouldn’t exist!” he fired back, voice raised. He contributed his reputation, his name (he literally named the company), and his early vision when no one else was willing to bet big on safe AGI. Those things have real value — way beyond just writing checks.

Savitt also drilled into whether OpenAI used Elon’s money for rent at the Pioneer Building (which Elon was leasing and sharing space with Neuralink). Elon confirmed he was on the hook for the full lease but would’ve found another tenant anyway. Classic “gotcha” attempt that landed flat.

Elon’s bottom line: $38 million is still a lot of money, and his non-cash contributions credibility, branding, foundational push were massive. OpenAI didn’t bootstrap itself in a vacuum.

This trial keeps exposing the tension: one side wants to reduce everything to ledger lines, the other is fighting over principles, mission, and who actually built the foundation. Elon’s not just defending his donations he’s defending the idea that you can’t rewrite history and turn a nonprofit promise into a closed, profit-driven empire without consequences.

Truth is, without Elon’s early involvement, OpenAI probably never gets off the ground the way it did. Reputation and vision aren’t nothing they’re everything in the early days of something this ambitious.

Stay tuned. This one’s far from over.

NEWS: Elon Musk grilled about his contributions to OpenAI during cross-examination on day 3.

OpenAI lawyer William Savitt pressed Elon Musk to confirm his donations totaled $38 million, far short of the "up to $1 billion" he had originally offered.

"Without me, OpenAI wouldn't exist!" Elon Musk said, raising his voice. "I contributed my reputation!" He added that he also named the company, saying "these things all have value."

Savitt also questioned whether OpenAI used Elon Musk's donations to pay rent at the Pioneer Building, which he leased and shared with Neuralink. 

Elon Musk confirmed he was on the hook for the entire lease but said he would have found another sub-tenant if not OpenAI.

Elon Musk maintained that "$38 million is still a lot of money" and the value of his contributions to OpenAI was worth much more.

On the left Elon Musk and on the right William Savitt

This is real unsupervised FSD in action at the factory. Mind officially blown.
